1.explanation:
• AccordionItem.js: This is the core file that renders the header button, title text, and chevron icon. It needs to accept the new `align` prop, default to “end”, and conditionally reverse the order (or apply a modifier class) when `align='start'`.
• Accordion.js: The wrapper should forward any unknown props (including alignment) to its child AccordionItems, or define `propTypes` for `align` at the Accordion level if desired.
• Accordion-story.js: Storybook needs an example showing both `align='start'` and `align='end'` so users can preview the new prop in the docs.
• AccordionItem-test.js & snapshot: The existing unit tests and snapshots assume chevron always appears at the end. They must be updated to render both alignments and to update the stored snapshots accordingly.

By changing these files we will fully support the new `align` prop in both code and documentation/tests.
1.bug_scenario:
The current Carbon AccordionItem always renders the expand/collapse chevron icon at the end of the header text. In our IBM Security wrapper we added an `align="start"` prop so the chevron appears on the left side of the header (our default), but Carbon’s AccordionItem only supports the default `end` alignment. The attached screenshot shows an AccordionItem with `align="start"`, where the chevron sits to the left of “Section 1 title”.

To upstream this feature we need to add an `align` prop (start|end) to the React AccordionItem, apply a CSS modifier or reverse the icon/text order in the render method when `align="start"`, and update the storybook demo and unit tests to cover both alignments.

2.explanation:
1. AccordionItem.js – this is where the React wrapper renders the chevron icon and title. It needs to be updated to accept and propagate the new align prop (defaulting to 'end'), add a class modifier (e.g. `${prefix}--accordion__item--align-start`), and conditionally render the icon before or after the title based on the prop.
2. Accordion-story.js – the story needs an example demonstrating align='start' (with the updated rendering) so consumers can see and test the new feature in Storybook.
3. __tests__/AccordionItem-test.js – the unit test for AccordionItem must be updated (and its snapshot) to include cases for align='start' so that the new rendering order and class modifier are correctly asserted.
2.bug_scenario: The wrapped AccordionItem component now accepts an optional “align” prop that controls whether the chevron (arrow icon) appears at the start of the heading or at the end. In the current implementation the chevron is always rendered at the end (Carbon’s default). The bug scenario shows two AccordionItems both passed align=“start”, but the chevron remains at the end. We need to update the React wrapper for AccordionItem to read the align prop, swap the order of the icon and title when align=“start”, add a modifier class, and update the story and tests to cover the new behavior.
